normalizedStops.law: STATIC ARM ONLY, NOT RECEIPTED (F4B-8/W-A/W-B law: an identity stop is a claim about what the VERTICAL ships; the DB arm takes no baseline by law and a single-arm run structurally cannot pass this evidence kind -- ingressEquivalenceHeld requires 2 comparable arms, same structural limit F4B-13/F4B-14 already measured for their own identity stops). rottay authors `recipes: RECIPES` where `const RECIPES: BrandRecipeSelection = { schemaVersion: 1, profile: 'rottay/technical-sharp@1' }` (rottay/index.ts:3289). Stated as a directly-compiled fact, not receipted evidence.

STATIC ARM ONLY, NOT RECEIPTED (same law as rottay/identity above). bithire authors `recipes: RECIPES` where `const RECIPES: BrandRecipeSelection = { schemaVersion: 1, profile: 'rottay/network-professional@1' }` (bithire/index.ts:3172) -- selecting an id namespaced 'rottay/...' is not a defect: the namespace names the REGISTRY's own provenance (foundation/tokens/ts/presentation/recipe-profiles), not which vertical may select it. evnto authors NO `recipes` field at all in its exported `evntoBrandTheme` (grep-confirmed: only a comment placeholder, `@governor none -- gap aceptado: capability recipes no autorada en evnto`) -- a genuine, explicit gap, not identity by absence-of-evidence, so evnto has no identity stop for this control.

calibration.coincidentalIdentityExclusionNote: Measured, not guessed: 2 of the 9 (stop x vertical) combinations are structurally excluded from the DB arm, not just non-movers. `rottay/technical-sharp@1` against rottay, and `rottay/network-professional@1` against bithire, are each that VERTICAL'S OWN authored identity -- writing the SAME value through the DB tenant document makes the compiler's own artifact-diff elide the channel entirely: the DB arm throws `StopExclusionError` (class COMPILER_ELIDES_VERTICAL_DEFAULT, a recognised, publishable exclusion) with 'emitted none of the declared channels ... in ANY scope -- not in the base map and not in any mode block'. The static arm does not crash but shows the same underlying fact differently: `moved=0`, byte-identical to the baseline (measured directly, both combinations). This is a STRONGER version of the same class typography.pairing already named for bithire/sober (F4B-11) -- there the DB arm still emitted the channel, unmoved; here it does not emit at all. Excluded from the receipted matrix for this reason (7 of 9 combinations receipted: technical-sharp x {bithire,evnto}, network-professional x {rottay,evnto}, editorial-round x all 3 -- editorial-round is nobody's identity, so it alone reaches all 3 verticals cleanly).
calibration.negativeControlsScopeNote: `font metrics remain fixed` is deliberately NOT declared for this control: --ds-recipe-profile is pure selection provenance (a quoted id string, never consumed by any live CSS reader -- see witnessScopeNote), so asserting a font-metrics negative control here would assert against a property this control has no mechanism to move in the first place, not a meaningful boundary. The 4 declared negatives hold trivially for the same reason -- the channel this control writes shares no consume site with color/geometry/typography/motion because it has no consume site at all yet.
calibration.witnessScopeNote: DT RULING (F4B-15): the witness is documented by the TWO real surfaces, with their exact scopes, rather than one field implying a single closed loop that does not exist. (a) --ds-recipe-profile (CSS): emitted in the compiled artifacts of rottay/bithire (facade/artifacts/rottay/index.css:767, facade/artifacts/bithire/index.css:817) -- grep-confirmed, NO production CSS file or component reads it; the compiler's own comment (brand-theme/index.ts:2071-2072) calls it selection provenance, published for whoever mounts it, not paint. (b) RecipeProfileProvider (JS, provider/index.tsx): a real, functioning consumer, but of `resolvedRuntimeConfig.appearance?.recipeProfile` (the DB-normalized TenantAppearance shape) -- NEVER of the CSS channel this control declares, and NEVER populated for the 3 code-owned verticals (today's actual production): `getCodeOwnedRuntimeConfig` (tenant/foundation/configuration/registry/index.ts:155-162) destructures `appearance` OUT of the projected config and never restores it, and the one alternate channel motion/expressive ride (`governedBehavior`, `projectGovernedBehavior` in the same file) does not carry `recipes` either -- verified by reading its body, only `motion`/`expressive` are handled. The two surfaces are architecturally decoupled; this is not a defect this control's own write-set can fix, and no consumer was invented to paper over it (D-1b law).
calibration.recipesFloorAsymmetryNote: `tenantPostureFloors` does NOT project `recipes` (only typography/surfaces/motion, tenant-theme/index.ts:1830-1844) -- the DB arm's composition of `recipes` depends ENTIRELY on `resolveTheme`'s generic `mergeDeep` (tenant-theme/index.ts:2007), with no E-1/W-B-style floor re-applying it at the end of `compileTheme`. Measured as sufficient for this control's own shape (W-B's argument, reused): there is no vertical-authored 'ladder' for recipe selection that could out-rank a tenant's own choice post-merge the way surfaces.elevation or typography's pairing preset could -- a real asymmetry against the other floored fields, named here rather than silently matched to their pattern.
